title: What the Coverage Share Acts On in a Standing Automatic Payment
content:
What the coverage share acts on, when a fixed monthly sum is settled on a card under Personal Credit Cards, turns on the money the cardholder moves through Personal Checking and on whether Personal Checking has charged them a fee.

*Where Piedmont Crescent Bank checking deposits posted to the cardholder's checking accounts in the last six months total at least 12000.00 USD and no Piedmont Crescent Bank checking fee was posted to those accounts in the last six months* — the coverage share acts on the payable balance together with the interest billed to the card account in the last month.

*Where those deposits total at least 12000.00 USD and at least one Piedmont Crescent Bank checking fee was posted to those accounts in the last six months* — the coverage share acts on the payable balance less the merchant credits posted to the card account in the last six months.

*Where those deposits total less than 12000.00 USD* — the coverage share acts on the payable balance alone.

**What each convention is worth.** On a hypothetical payable balance of 1799.37 USD, interest of 128.60 USD billed to the card account in the last month and merchant credits of 60.00 USD posted to it in the last six months, the first convention acts on 1927.97 USD, the second on 1739.37 USD and the third on 1799.37 USD.

**On the boundaries.** The deposit figure is read as at least, so deposits of exactly 12000.00 USD in the last six months belong with the higher band and 11999.00 USD with the lower, where the count of checking fees is not reached at all. One checking fee in the window is enough to move a high-deposit cardholder from the first convention to the second.
